problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/2e8eee199131d64b8772e15acb848030ac810cc96fd20b4f75005e5aab2770ed.png)

A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=4$ in the first quadrant.
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=2.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 2},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/f5a73161415455032a7fd2031dba8f1c56a7ccb40bf6dc3e4fa405a69aee74d8.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $y=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y-2|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|x|=kx,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}kx\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}x[y]_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}x(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{2}(4x-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{[2{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =k(8-4) \\  & =4k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=kx=\frac{M}{4}x.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\frac{M}{4}x\cdot |y-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\frac{M}{4}x\cdot (y-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}x{[\frac{(y-2)^{3}}{3}]}_{{x}^{2}}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}x(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{({x}^{2}-2)^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{2}(8x-x({x}^{2}-2)^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-{x}^{7}+6{x}^{5}-12{x}^{3}+16)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{[-\frac{{x}^{8}}{8}+{x}^{6}-3{x}^{4}+16x]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{M}{12}(-32+64-48+32) \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13

A plate with mass M occupies the region D enclosed between the curves y=x2 and y=4 in the first quadrant. The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the y-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line y=2.

a
3M8
b
3M5
c
4M3
d
M4
e
8M5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region D about an axis of rotation l is given by

Il=∬Dλ(x,y)[r(x,y)]2dA,

where λ(x,y) is the mass density function of the lamina, and r(x,y) is the distance from the line l to the point (x,y) on D.

First, notice that D is a type I region with representation

D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,x2≤y≤2},

as shown below.

Also, the distance between a point and the line y=2 is given by

r(x,y)=|y−2|.

Next, the mass density can be written as λ(x,y)=k|x|=kx, where k is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of k by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

M=∬Dλ(x,y)dA=∫02∫x24kxdydx=k∫02x[y]x24dx=k∫02x(4−x2)dx=k∫02(4x−x3)dx=k[2x2−14x4]02=k(8−4)=4k.

Hence,

λ(x,y)=kx=M4x.

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line y=2 is

Il=∬Dλ(x,y)[r(x,y)]2dA=∫02∫x24M4x⋅|y−2|2dydx=∫02∫x24M4x⋅(y−2)2dydx=M4∫02x[(y−2)33]x24dx=M4∫02x(83−(x2−2)33)dx=M12∫02(8x−x(x2−2)3)dx=M12∫02(−x7+6x5−12x3+16)dx=M12[−x88+x6−3x4+16x]02=M12(−32+64−48+32)=4M3.
